title: BrewJSON house profile
description: One brewhouse: its equipment sets and process numbers. Draft-07 to match BeerJSON 1.0.

default_equipment.description: Id of the equipment set new batches use unless told otherwise.

HouseWaterType.description: The source water, which recipes' water figures (salts, ions, mash pH) start from. Absent: tools assume a typical supply.

profile.description: Ions in mg/L (bicarbonate = alkalinity as CaCO3 x 1.22) and pH.

typical.description: True while the profile is a typical supply standing in for a water report.

disinfectant.description: Chloramine doesn't boil or stand off; it needs Campden.

calcium_chloride.description: The form of calcium chloride the house uses.

acid.description: The acid the house uses to lower mash pH.

ProcessType.description: The brewhouse's planning numbers, for recipe calcs. Equipment figures (losses, boil-off, grain absorption) live on the equipment items.

mash_efficiency.description: Grain to kettle at the end of the boil: the planning figure. OG = grist potential x this / end-of-boil volume.

mash_water.description: Mash water = grist mass x per_kg + plus.

exclude.description: Fermentables left out of the grist mass, by name (e.g. Rice Hulls).

whirlpool_temperature.description: Deprecated, and ignored by brewday: the whirlpool temperature is a recipe choice, given on the recipe's whirlpool boil step. Accepted in 0.2 so existing files stay valid; removed in the next version.

max_grist.description: Above this the mash suffers (efficiency drops); recipe tools warn.

EquipmentSetType.description: A BeerJSON equipment set with the id BeerJSON doesn't give it. A batch snapshots the equipment object and records the id.
